results.title: [PDF] Guideline on adjustment for baseline covariates in clinical trials
results.content: Guideline on adjustment for baseline covariates in clinical trials EMA/CHMP/295050/2013 Page 4/11 • The primary model should not include treatment by covariate interactions. Note that when the baseline is included as a covariate in a standard Guideline on adjustment for baseline covariates in clinical trials EMA/CHMP/295050/2013 Page 8/11 linear model, the estimated treatment effects are identical for both ‘change from baseline’ (on an additive scale) and the ‘raw outcome’ analysis. If the conclusions from the primary analysis and the sensitivity analyses are very different in terms of clinical and statistical significance and the difference cannot be explained by e.g. imbalances between treatment groups in the covariates, then the results of the trial could become inconclusive.

results.content: Home  /  Products  /  Features  /  Balance analysis for treatment effects. # Balance analysis for treatment effects. * Test for balance for inverse-probability-weighted estimators. * Comparison of model-adjusted covariate distributions across treatment groups. Treatment-effects estimators for observational data use a variety of techniques, including reweighting and matching, to achieve experimental-like balanced data results. We can examine whether the treatment model balanced the covariates and perform a statistical test. 1. One diagnostic reports, for each covariate, the model-adjusted difference in means in the treatment groups and the ratio of variances. 2. Another diagnostic graphs the model-adjusted estimated densities of covariates; these densities can be examined visually to verify that they are approximately equal.
